subject: Planned: Deferred kernel switchover for eastus3 — Sept 6–8 (rolling, low-impact)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: CloudPlatform Ops <ops@acme.io>, acme-infra@acme.io
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Planned: Deferred kernel switchover for eastus3 — Sept 6–8 (rolling, low-impact)

Hi team,

We wanted to give you early notice of a scheduled maintenance window affecting eastus3. This is a deferred kernel/driver switchover intended to address a rare IO path regression we observed in a subset of instances. Our goal is to perform the work with rolling restarts and minimal customer impact.

Planned window (primary):
- Start: Mon, Sep 6 00:00 UTC
- End: Wed, Sep 8 23:59 UTC
- Expected per-host downtime: ~120s (graceful restart)
- Approach: sequenced rolling restarts by host-pool with KV cache preservation and warm handovers

What to expect:
- We will route traffic away from hosts as they are restarted; live inference will be routed to healthy hosts.
- Short-lived in-flight requests may be retried automatically by the client SDKs; please make sure your retries/backoff are enabled for idempotent calls.
- We will not change model versions or rollback behavior during this window.

Attachments: deferred-switchover-maintenance-plan.pdf (outline + host ordering), kv-cache-preservation-checklist.xlsx (internal checklist).

Action items for Acme:
1) Confirm if you have any single-host pinned workloads in eastus3 that require evacuation prior to Sep 6.
2) Provide any maintenance blackout windows we must avoid.

We will share a detailed per-hour schedule and the final host sequence on Tue Sep 1. If you'd like a dedicated runbook review, Marissa can coordinate a short call next week.

Thanks,
Jonas

-- 
Jonas Weber
Senior Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199
From: CloudPlatform Ops <ops@acme.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:15:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Planned: Deferred kernel switchover for eastus3 — Sept 6–8 (rolling, low-impact)

Jonas,

Thanks for the heads up. A few quick questions from our side:

- Can you confirm whether persistent volumes attached to inference hosts will reattach automatically, or should we pre-drain pods that rely on local storage?
- Will there be any change to the public endpoint certificates or IP addresses? We need to rule out potential TLS/connection churn.
- If we see elevated 5xxs during a host restart window, is there an L2 (pager) escalation path?

We have a maintenance blackout for our billing batch on Sep 7 from 02:00–04:00 UTC; please avoid scheduling any restarts that target our primary host-pool in that interval.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
CloudPlatform Ops — Acme Corp
ops@acme.io

Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 12:02:35 -0400
Subject: Re: Planned: Deferred kernel switchover for eastus3 — internal runbook notes

Folks — internal follow-up before we reply to Acme's questions:

- Persistent volumes: host restarts are graceful; attached GPV/remote volumes will reattach. For customers using local NVMe scratch, we recommend they pre-stage any critical state off-host. Will note this in the runbook.
- No cert/IP changes — we will preserve public endpoints and cert chains (TLS unchanged).
- Pager: I'll add Ben to the L2 rotation for the affected window; L2 escalation will be via PagerDuty (PD: REDWOOD-ops, escalation policy #3).

Proposed response to Acme: confirm volume behavior, commit to avoiding their Sep 7 02:00–04:00 UTC billing blackout for their primary host-pool, and offer a 30-min runbook walk-through on Tue Sep 1 14:00 UTC.

I attached the checklist for quick reference.

-Marissa

Attachments: kv-cache-preservation-checklist.xlsx
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: CloudPlatform Ops <ops@acme.io>, acme-infra@acme.io
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, GCP Partner <gcp-partner@partnercloud.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Planned: Deferred kernel switchover for eastus3 — schedule and answers

Hi Aisha — thanks for the questions and the blackout window. Answers below: 

1) Persistent volumes: for standard network-backed volumes (GPV/NFS/S3-backed), these will reattach automatically after the node restarts. For any workloads that write to ephemeral local NVMe, we advise off-host state or pre-drain.

2) Certs/IPs: no changes to TLS certs or public IPs. Connection handoffs are handled at the load-balancer layer.

3) Escalation: L2 will be on-call and reachable via PagerDuty (REDWOOD-ops). If you prefer an on-call phone escalation, let us know and we can arrange it for the window.

Blackout: we will not schedule restarts that impact your primary host-pool during Sep 7 02:00–04:00 UTC. We have updated the per-hour plan accordingly.

Runbook review: we propose Tue Sep 1 14:00 UTC for a 30-minute run-through. Invite: https://meet.google.com/redwood-acme-runbook

Public schedule snapshot (per-host-pool approximate):
- Sep 6 00:00–12:00 UTC: host-pools A & B (non-primary first pass)
- Sep 6 12:00–Sep 7 00:00 UTC: host-pools C & D
- Sep 7 00:00–18:00 UTC: primary host-pool (avoid 02:00–04:00 UTC)
- Sep 8: staggered catch-up / verification and targeted rechecks

Attachments: deferred-switchover-maintenance-plan.pdf (detailed host order + mitigation steps)

Please confirm the runbook time or propose an alternate slot.

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
From: CloudPlatform Ops <ops@acme.io>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 19:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Planned: Deferred kernel switchover for eastus3 — schedule and answers

Jonas / Marissa,

Appreciate the clarifications and the change to avoid our blackout. We accept the proposed window and will join the runbook review Tue Sep 1 14:00 UTC (we received the calendar invite). A couple of small asks before the window:

- Could you include a short guidance bullet in the runbook for SDK retry tuning (recommended timeout + backoff settings for Acme workloads)?
- Please confirm whether the per-host expected downtime is still ~120s in your final doc.

We'll monitor for the calendar invite but otherwise good to proceed.

Thanks,
Aisha
CloudPlatform Ops — Acme Corp
